chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Charley Johnson and the Paradise
summary: Wooding praises Johnson as the best cabaret organizer who made Weloff's Paradise famous and later came to New York with Smalls.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Uh hunh. But, Charley Johnson, at that point didn't have a band, he was just working as a pianist. Is that right?
Yeah, he was working as a pianist. But he had charge of -- now he, Charley, this was one of our great-est cabaret runners. He's the one that made the name "Paradise".

Cause there was an owner down there named Max Weloff, Ray Weloff. And Ray Weloff had this Paradise down at Atlantic City. And Charley made it into a legend. And people come from all over to go to the Ray Weloff's Paradise. And for Charley Johnson. Then when Ray went out of the business, Charley came to New York with Smalls, and they again used the name Paradise. And so, now he's got a new life, and 'til today people speak of Small's Paradise. But it really should have been Charley Johnson's Paradise.
Because he's the one that made it, see.
Uh hunh. But what did you think of him as a pianist?

Not a great pianist. But a great gentleman. You know, every great gentleman can't fight. I mean as for prizefighting or physically fighting an enemy. But he had the brains. Noone has ever, Eubie Blake or nobody else has never been comparable to Charley Johnson for knowing how to engineer a successful cabaret, and with entertainers and all.
So he was a good businessman.
And he had a good band too.
His band was one of the greatest.
Now you, so you ran into Charley Johnson, and you became friends, I guess.
